title: How to validate an automated colony counter
protocol: Prepare each culture medium according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Autoclave and cool culture medium to 47±2°C.
Supplement Columbia Agar with 5% v/v defibrinated horse blood after autoclaving.
Pour culture medium into sterile 9cm Petri dishes.
Leave plates to set and dry.

Sub-culture each bacterial or fungal culture from frozen stocks onto the appropriate agar medium: P. aeruginosa, E.coli, S. aureus, K. rhizophila, E. faecalis, B.subtilis on PCA; M. haemolytica, S. pneumoniae on CBA; A. brasiliensis and C. albicans on SDA.
Incubate plate cultures at 37°C for approximately 24 h (bacterial strains), at 30°C for approximately 48 h (C. albicans) or at 30°C for 7 days (A. brasiliensis).
Collect from 3 to 5 colonies on the incubated plate for each strain, except A. brasiliensis.
Suspend cells in sterile MRD.
Vortex mix cell suspension to produce turbidity equivalent to that of a 0.5 McFarland standard, containing approximately 1.0×108 CFU/ml.
Flood the plate surface with MRD so that fungal hyphae are emulsified for A. brasiliensis.
Pipette from the plate into a sterile vial.
Prepare serial decimal dilutions in MRD, to a final level of 10-7 of each bacterial and fungal suspension.
Apply dilutions of each bacterial or fungal strain to the surface of the appropriate agar plates using spiral plating.
Apply a 50 μl volume of each dilution 10-2, 10-3, and 10-4 on each of the appropriate agar plates for spiral plates.
Apply a 0.5 ml volume of each dilution 10-5, 10-6, and 10-7 to the appropriate agar plate for spread plates.
Distribute the inoculum with a sterile plastic “hockey stick” spreader on the spread plates.
Incubate plate cultures at 37°C for approximately 24 h (bacterial strains).
Incubate plate cultures at 30°C for approximately 48 h (_C. albicans_).
Incubate plate cultures at 30°C for 4 days (_A. brasiliensis_) to ensure the formation of discrete colonies.
Select a single incubated plate from each spiral plate and spread plate series where single discrete colonies are obtained.
Place each selected plate on the ProtoCOL 3 stage.
Configure the instrument in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
Insert the black plate to remove lower illumination for reading CBA plates of _M. haemolytica_ and _S. pneumoniae_.
Adjust software settings to count touching colonies as well as light colonies on a dark background or dark colonies on a light background, as appropriate.
Read spiral plates using the spiral frame setting with two sectors.
Read spread plates using the circular counting frame.
Count colonies on both spiral and spread plates.
Analyse the manual and automated counts for each plate type using a two-tailed t-test for paired samples.
Use log CFU/ml figures for spiral plate data to ensure normally distributed data.
Compare raw colony counts per frame for spread plate data.
Conduct t-tests for spiral and spread plates.
